name: attachment
title: Attachment
description: Displays file media, metadata, caller-owned upload state, and actions.
docs: ## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/attachment ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Attachment, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentContent, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentActions, AttachmentAction, } from "@/components/cadence/attachment"; export function FileCard({ onRemove }: { onRemove: () => void }) { return ( PDF report.pdf PDF · 2.4 MB × ); } ``` ## Upload state Pass `state="idle"`, `"uploading"`, `"processing"`, `"error"` or `"done"` from your application. Uploading and processing pulse the title; the description carries readable status even with animation disabled. An error needs text explaining the failure. Set `aria-busy` on the appropriate region and use a separate polite status for meaningful milestones, rather than announcing every progress update. ```tsx report.pdf Uploading · 64% ``` ## Images and sizes Use `AttachmentMedia variant="image"` with a native image and meaningful alt text. `orientation="vertical"` stacks it above the metadata; horizontal is the default. Sizes are `default`, `sm` and `xs`. The media is dimmed while work is in progress. Supply image URLs yourself; the component never creates or revokes object URLs. ## Trigger and independent actions `AttachmentTrigger` fills the card behind `AttachmentActions`. Give the empty trigger an accessible name. It defaults to a non-submitting button; `render` accepts an element or render function, preserving Base UI event/ref merging. Actions default to ghost Button with icon-xs size and accept Button's callbacks, native props and `render`. Keep actions in AttachmentActions so their stacking order leaves them independently reachable. ```tsx } /> ``` ## Scrollable groups Wrap cards in `AttachmentGroup` for a snapping horizontal row. Native scrolling is immediate and never smoothed by this component. For presentational cards give the group `tabIndex={0}`, `role="group"` and an accessible name; interactive cards can be reached with Tab. Allow the group to shrink within its parent. ```tsx workspace.png ``` ## When to use File previews in composers, upload lists, or message attachments with caller-owned metadata and optional open/remove/retry actions. ## When not to use Use Input for native file selection, Progress for a standalone percentage, and Item for generic content that does not represent a file. Attachment does not implement an uploader, drop zone, file parser or streaming message runtime. ## API | Part | Props and defaults | | --- | --- | | `Attachment` | Native div props; state `done`, size `default`, orientation `horizontal` | | `AttachmentMedia` | Native div props; variant `icon` or `image`, default `icon` | | `AttachmentContent` | Native div props; wraps metadata | | `AttachmentTitle` | Native span props; filename, busy opacity loop | | `AttachmentDescription` | Native span props; metadata/status text | | `AttachmentActions` | Native div props; independent action layer | | `AttachmentAction` | All Button props; size `icon-xs`, variant falls back to `ghost` | | `AttachmentTrigger` | Base UI useRender button props; type `button` without render; render element/function | | `AttachmentGroup` | Native div props; horizontal scroll and snap | Every part preserves its upstream `attachment-*` data-slot (root: `attachment`). Native refs, styles and events pass through; classes merge last. Root also exposes `data-state`, `data-size`, `data-orientation`; media exposes `data-variant`. No File or request state is stored internally. There is no default upload action. ## Motion contract | Cause | Recipe | Full | Reduced | None | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Uploading/processing title | `data.transition` | Opacity pulse via theme `animate-pulse` | Same opacity loop, no transform | `animate-none`, opacity 1 | | Default action pressed | `feedback.press` | Button token spring/press scale | No scale | Instant, no scale | Continuous timing comes from the project's `--animate-pulse` theme token. This replaces upstream's travelling shimmer with opacity to stay in the motion budget. Root/title and default actions expose `data-motion`; live none cancels the loop without replacing nodes. State, removal, size, orientation and media updates are immediate. No entry, exit, layout or geometry recipe is implied. Custom render controls can own their own feedback as with Button. ## Keyboard interactions Tab reaches triggers and actions separately. Enter/Space activate default buttons; a rendered link uses native link behaviour. Disabled actions retain Button's native semantics. A focusable group scrolls with arrow keys; Tab also reveals off-screen interactive cards. Removal focus policy belongs to the caller. ## Accessibility Name every icon-only action and overlay trigger, retain meaningful image alt text, and describe failures in text. The trigger has a visible focus ring. Avoid nested interactive elements inside triggers. Provide a polite live region for upload milestones outside a busy region. Truncated filenames remain in the DOM; a title attribute or your own details view can expose their full visual text. ## Validation and data ownership The application owns native file input `name`, `accept`, `multiple`, `required`, File objects, form submission, validation, upload progress, requests, cancel/retry, URLs and URL cleanup. Attachment forwards `aria-invalid`/`data-invalid` when given; `state="error"` only styles a supplied failure. It never decides which file is valid. The preview's file input reports the selected filename locally and makes no request. ## Responsiveness and performance Cards cap at their parent's width; long names truncate. Groups scroll horizontally with no document overflow when their parent can shrink. Large lists should be paginated or virtualized by the application. The busy opacity loop uses CSS with no per-frame JavaScript or layout reads; none stops it on the next style update. No @shadcn/react dependency or streaming runtime is needed for this pinned API. ## AI usage notes Compose these nine parts; keep upload state and file lifecycle in your application. Do not infer a network operation from the visual `state` value. Prefer stable file IDs as keys so a progress update preserves focus and the native input. There is no message streaming dependency and no reason to remount a composer when a file changes. ## Related components [Button](/components/button) supplies actions, [Input](/components/input) supplies native file selection, [Progress](/components/progress) displays known progress, and [Code Block](/components/code-block) displays textual file contents.
